HEATH_BROWN_BINDING.author: D. R. Heath-Brown
HEATH_BROWN_BINDING.title: Artin's conjecture for primitive roots
HEATH_BROWN_BINDING.theorem_used: At least one of 2, 3, 5 is a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes.
HEATH_BROWN_BINDING.scope_note: Only this unconditional external number-theory theorem is imported; no Artin conjecture, GRH, density theorem, SHA heuristic, or probabilistic statement is used.

INFINITE_SMALL_g_SUBSEQUENCE_PROOF.definition: g_p is the least integer primitive root modulo p from the frozen family definition.
proof: Heath-Brown gives infinitely many primes for which at least one a in {2,3,5} is a primitive root; equivalently the union of the three corresponding prime sets is infinite.
For every such prime p, the least primitive root satisfies g_p<=a<=5, hence p belongs to P_star except for finitely many excluded small primes.
Therefore P_star is infinite and unbounded.
Removing all p<=4*5^14 leaves an infinite subsequence P_star_star.
INFINITE_SMALL_g_SUBSEQUENCE_PROOF.consequence_for_slopes: For p in P_star_star and j=0,...,14, 1<=g_p^j<=5^14<p, so the frozen residues s_j=g_p^j mod p equal the ordinary integers g_p^j.

BOUNDED_WIDTH_DECOMPOSITION.graph: G_p=Inc(F_p) with 18 vertex types A,B,C,E_0,...,E_14 over cyclic coordinate Z_p

fixed_type_cyclic_span_lemma.statement: If a graph has at most t vertices in each Z_p coordinate fibre, every edge has circular coordinate span at most R, and p>2R, then pathwidth <= t*(3R+1)-1.
fixed_type_cyclic_span_lemma.proof: Cut at coordinate 0. Put every vertex in the first R and last R fibres into a persistent boundary S, so |S|<=2tR. Outside S, an edge of circular span <=R cannot wrap and hence has ordinary span <=R. For consecutive interior coordinates i, use bag B_i=S union fibres i,...,i+R. Every edge is covered; each nonboundary vertex appears in a contiguous interval of bags; boundary vertices appear in all bags. Thus |B_i|<=2tR+t(R+1)=t(3R+1).

instantiation.scope: For every p in the infinite subsequence P_star_star.

WL_FALSIFICATION_VERDICT.frozen_claim: sep_2_3(G_p)=omega(log p), hence tw(G_p)=omega(log p), along the full prime-indexed family p>=17
WL_FALSIFICATION_VERDICT.proof: Along infinite unbounded P_star_star, tw(G_p)<=C. Hence tw(G_p)/log p ->0 along that subsequence, contradicting omega(log p) along all primes. Also the standard treewidth balanced-separator theorem gives sep_2_3(G_p)<=C+1 on P_star_star, so sep_2_3(G_p)/log p ->0 there.
WL_FALSIFICATION_VERDICT.important_nonclaim: This does not rule out another subsequence of the same family having larger width; it falsifies only the frozen uniform-all-primes WL statement and blocks this whole prime-indexed family as the currently preregistered uniform witness.

SURVIVING_THEOREMS: The current family remains an infinite reducer-fixpoint family even though it has an infinite bounded-treewidth subsequence.

FAILED_FAMILY_REQUIREMENT.witness: Heath-Brown implies infinitely many p with g_p<=5, forcing all 15 frozen shifts to lie in [1,5^14] as ordinary integers for sufficiently large such p.
FAILED_FAMILY_REQUIREMENT.representation_independent_restatement: The selected structural witness must not possess an infinite subsequence admitting a uniformly bounded-width/pathwidth certificate from a fixed-type cyclic layout.
FAILED_FAMILY_REQUIREMENT.warning: Avoiding this escape is necessary for the intended uniform superlog-width witness program but is not sufficient to prove any treewidth lower bound.
